subject: Multi-locale qualification: EU/APAC next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Ho <peter.ho@linguatech.com>, Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@finserve.de>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-locale qualification: EU/APAC next steps

Hi Peter / Anna —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next steps to move the evaluation forward: 

TL;DR: we recommend a short POC (2–3 weeks) focused on two critical flows: transaction reconciliation (DE, FR) and customer chat triage (JP, EN-AU). We’ll run model A/B on candidate families and provide per-locale quality metrics + cost/latency breakdown.

Call notes:
- Main goals: reduce false-positive routing in chat; improve named-entity extraction for financial references in German and French.
- Constraints: sample data includes masked PII, but we need 5–10 representative transcripts per locale to sanity-check prompts.
- Success criteria (provisional): intent accuracy >= 92% for chat triage; NER F1 >= 0.86 on held-out German/French set.

Recommended initial model candidates (we’ll surface config + quantization):
1) Open-Delta-7B (quantized 4-bit) — strong latency/cost balance for chat triage; likely best for JP when trimmed with locale-specific prompt templates.
2) L-Large-13B (8-bit) — better generative quality for long reconciliation explanations; higher cost but fewer hallucinations in financial text.
3) Redwood-3B-finetuned-lang — a small finetune we can run quickly on your masked dataset to validate prompt-sensitivity.

Deliverables we propose for the POC (Redwood):
- Model benchmark report (per-locale precision/recall, latency P50/P95, token cost) — link included below.
- Prompt set v1 for each flow (attached: prompt_set_v1.md).
- Small evaluation harness with seed prompts and automated regression checks.
- Deployment plan: Hosted API for initial validation, then Dedicated pool for scale if throughput looks good.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Peter: share 10 sample transcripts per target locale (DE, FR, JP) by Tue 2027-04-06. (Peter)
- Neha: spin up A/B jobs + share benchmark template by Thu 2027-04-08. (Neha)
- Sergio: prepare commercial outline and preliminary pricing for POC and 6-mo Dedicated option. (Sergio)
- Vivek: brief on potential SLA exceptions for APAC on-call window (internal). (Vivek)

Attachments: locale_sample_pack.zip (placeholder) contains our recommended schema + sample masking script; prompt_set_v1.md; benchmark_report_EU_Q1.pdf (previously run for a similar finance partner).

If this matches your expectations I’ll schedule the POC kickoff for Wednesday and share a short MLP (mutual action plan).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Peter Ho <peter.ho@linguatech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@finserve.de>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Multi-locale qualification: EU/APAC next steps

Hi Neha —

Thanks, this is helpful. 2 quick clarifications:
1) For the 10 transcripts per locale, should these include both voice->text and human-chat logs or just one type?
2) Are you able to run a small-scale hallucination check (fact-consistency) on reconciliation flows? That’s a hard blocker for our compliance team.

We can share the samples by Tue evening SGT; they’ll be masked but preserve tokenization quirks. Also looping in our localization lead, Suzuki, who can help with JP examples.

— Peter
Director, Product — LinguaTech Solutions
Phone: +65 8123 4567

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-locale qualification: EU/APAC next steps — sample and plan

Peter / Anna / Suzuki —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A few updates after reviewing the sample pack you shared:

1) File types/formatting: we received both voice-derived transcripts and chat logs — that’s ideal. Please keep the original tokenization markers if possible (we rely on those for sequence-length profiles).

2) Hallucination check: yes, we’ll include a fact-consistency probe as part of the eval harness. We’ll run an automated pass and also surface human-review flags for ambiguous cases. Expect preliminary hallucination metrics in the first benchmark drop.

3) Model recommendations (refined):
- Candidate A (Open-Delta-7B q4) — baseline for cost-sensitive chat triage; will test with locale-specific prompt templates in JP and EN-AU.
- Candidate B (L-Large-13B 8-bit) — prioritized for reconciliation where long context comprehension matters; we’ll monitor tokenization edge cases in German compound nouns.
- Candidate C (Redwood-3B-ft-local) — we’ll run a lightweight finetune on masked reconciliation records if you’re comfortable with that. Finetune would be limited to 500–1,000 masked examples and is reversible.

4) Quality regression concerns:
- We’ll set up regression alerts tied to seed prompts (included in prompt_set_v1.md). If any candidate drops >5% absolute on the primary metric for a locale, the job will mark as failed and we’ll pause rollout.
- For DE/FR NER sensitivity, we recommend adding a small holdout of adversarial examples to detect tokenization-induced failures (I can share a short script).

Next steps:
- Sergio will send the POC commercial and T&Cs by EOD Thu.
- I’ll push the first benchmark run to Drive and link you once complete (expected by Fri 2027-04-09).
- Can Suzuki confirm JP character-encoding edge-cases by Fri? (Suzuki)

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.md (prompts + seed checks), locale_sample_pack.zip (schema + sample masked records).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi all —

We’ve reviewed the POC outline and are comfortable to proceed on the proposed scope. A couple of final asks from compliance:

- Please confirm the retention window for masked samples during the POC (we prefer 30 days post-completion).
- Provide a short runbook describing who has access to the evaluation artifacts and logs.

Once those are in writing we’ll confirm the kickoff date. Our legal team prefers an email note agreeing to the retention/controls rather than a full SOW for the initial POC.

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

Regards,
Anna Schmidt
Head of Compliance — FinServe DE
anna.schmidt@finserve.de
